source.title: Approximation by rational functions: Open problems.

accepted.question_text: Let E be a closed bounded subset of the complex plane whose complement is simply connected, and let G be the Green function of the complement of E with pole at infinity. For R>1, let E_R be the finite region bounded by the level curve G(z)=log R. In the classical theory discussed on the source page, if a function f is analytic on E and meromorphic in E_R with only finitely many poles, then there are rational-approximation results that parallel polynomial approximation theorems for best rational approximants R_{mn}. The open problem is to determine whether the corresponding approximation theory still holds when f is meromorphic in E_R but has infinitely many poles there instead of only finitely many poles.
accepted.context_brief: Rational approximation with infinitely many poles in E_R

evidence.page: zbMATH review text, main summary paragraph
evidence.quote: Some recent results on approximation by rational functions relate the table of rational functions (*) ... of best approximation to a given function f(z) on a closed bounded set E to approximation by polynomials, notably the case where E is a closed bounded set whose complement is simply connected and f(z) is analytic on E, meromorphic with ν poles in the finite region E_R bounded by the level locus G(z)=log R of Green’s function for the complement of E with pole at infinity. The corresponding problem where f(z) has an infinity of poles in E_R is open.

accepted.question_text: Suppose D is a region bounded by an analytic Jordan curve C, f is analytic in D and continuous on the closure D̄, and the p-th derivative f^(p) is Lipschitz of order α on C for some 0<α<1. For polynomial best approximation p_n of degree n one has a Jackson-type estimate ||f-p_n|| ≤ A/n^(p+α). The source states that Saff treated the analogous rational-approximation problem when the target function is meromorphic in E_R with only finitely many poles. The unsolved question is whether an analogous Jackson-type estimate remains valid when the function is meromorphic in E_R with infinitely many poles.
accepted.context_brief: Jackson-type rational approximation with infinitely many poles

evidence.page: zbMATH review text, main summary paragraph
evidence.quote: Likewise for the analogue of the Jacksonlike result that if f(z) is analytic in a region D bounded by an analytic Jordan curve C, continuous in D̄, and f^(p)(z) is Lipschitz on C of order α(0<α<1) then for best approximation by polynomials p_n(z) of resp. degrees n we have ||f(z)-p_n(z)|| ≤ A / n^{p+α}. The analogue for f(z) meromorphic in E_R with a finite number of poles was treated by Saff, but again the case of an infinite number of poles is unsolved.

accepted.question_text: For the rational functions of best approximation appearing in the Padé-style table R_{mn}, determine the location and distribution of their poles. More specifically, the source notes that several results related to the Padé table and to these best rational approximants are known, but the basic problem of identifying where the poles of the best approximants lie remains open.
accepted.context_brief: Pole locations of best rational approximants

evidence.page: zbMATH review text, final sentence of main summary paragraph
evidence.quote: Still other results connected with the Pade table and (*) are known; in each case the problem remains unsolved: Where are the poles of the rational functions of best approximation?
